dossier.purpose: Python package claude-agent-sdk 0.2.163 (pyproject.toml:6-7): starts the Claude Code CLI (`claude`) as a child process and drives it over a stream-JSON stdin/stdout control protocol (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py:570-795, 873-881). Offers query() and ClaudeSDKClient, in-process custom tools (SDK MCP servers), hook and permission callbacks, subagents, structured output, cost/usage in ResultMessage, and session list/resume/fork helpers with an optional external SessionStore mirror (src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:1609-1734, 1970-2437). Model calls, tool execution, sandbox, permission evaluation and subagents run inside the CLI, not this package; platform wheels bundle CLI 2.1.286 (src/claude_agent_sdk/_cli_version.py:3). Facts for the stated needs: (1) model choice is documented only for Claude models (types.py:2070-2074); no GPT/OpenAI/'Sol' reference exists in the repo (searched); (2) sandbox is optional, default-off, bash-only, macOS/Linux, forwarded to the CLI via --settings (types.py:904-950; subprocess_cli.py:473-525); (3) bounded access: tools/allowed_tools/disallowed_tools, six permission modes, can_use_tool, hooks, max_turns, max_budget_usd, task_budget (types.py:25-27, 1974-2068, 2430-2437); (4) resumability: resume/continue_conversation/fork_session over CLI transcripts in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.claude) plus optional session_store (types.py:2040-2048, 2249-2263, 2403-2428; src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/sessions.py:122-141); (5) no deep-research harness, citation model, worker pool or orchestrator exists; text blocks keep only `text` (types.py:954-958; _internal/message_parser.py:169-170). The README does not document sandbox, resume/session_store, model selection or authentication.

claims.claim: Python SDK for Claude Agent; full docs are at platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python (external page, not in this repo).
Install with `pip install claude-agent-sdk`; prerequisite Python 3.10+.

The Claude Code CLI is automatically bundled with the package, no separate installation required; the SDK uses the bundled CLI by default. For a system-wide install or specific version, install Claude Code separately or set ClaudeAgentOptions(cli_path=...).
query() is an async function for querying Claude Code, returning an AsyncIterator of response messages.

By default Claude has the full Claude Code toolset (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, others); allowed_tools is an auto-approve allowlist that does not remove tools, unlisted tools fall through to permission_mode and can_use_tool; disallowed_tools blocks tools.
permission_mode='acceptEdits' auto-accepts file edits; cwd sets the working directory.
The system prompt is recorded on a session's first request and reused on resume unless snapshot is False (needs Claude Code CLI 2.1.257+).
ClaudeSDKClient supports bidirectional, interactive conversations; unlike query() it additionally enables custom tools and hooks.
Custom tools are in-process MCP servers (no subprocess management, 'No IPC overhead for tool calls'); SDK and external stdio MCP servers can be mixed.
Hooks are Python functions the Claude Code application (not Claude) invokes at specific points of the agent loop, for deterministic processing and automated feedback.
Error classes include CLINotFoundError, CLIConnectionError, ProcessError, ResultError (terminal error result with subtype, terminal_reason, api_error_status) and CLIJSONDecodeError.

Manual release workflow takes version and claude_code_version (e.g. 2.0.0 or latest), builds macOS/Linux/Windows wheels bundling that CLI plus an sdist, publishes to PyPI, creates a release branch and opens a PR to main.
scripts/build_wheel.py downloads the Claude Code CLI for the platform, bundles it in the wheel, builds wheel and sdist, and checks with twine.
Use of the SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service, including for products built on it, except where a component's own LICENSE file says otherwise.

integrations.cli: none for the SDK itself - pyproject.toml declares no [project.scripts] (pyproject.toml:1-149). Wheels bundle the separate Claude Code `claude` binary (README.md:15; subprocess_cli.py:341-354), spawned with --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json (subprocess_cli.py:574, 793). scripts/*.py are release tooling, not packaged (pyproject.toml:62-64).
integrations.mcp: Host side only: in-process SDK MCP servers via @tool and create_sdk_mcp_server() (src/claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:251-335, 491-619), bridged to the CLI as mcp_message control requests (_internal/sdk_mcp_bridge.py:1-22; _internal/query.py:656-674); external stdio/SSE/HTTP configs pass through via --mcp-config (types.py:623-668; subprocess_cli.py:667-692). Server-initiated sampling, elicitation, roots, logging and progress are not forwarded (types.py:648-659). No MCP endpoint for outside clients found (no server or listening-socket code under src/).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK: query() (src/claude_agent_sdk/query.py:11-132) and ClaudeSDKClient (src/claude_agent_sdk/client.py:26-631), plus a Transport ABC the maintainers warn may change or be removed (_internal/transport/__init__.py:8-14). No HTTP API or server found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: this is its Python SDK - wraps the CLI (README.md:35, 99-100); exposes setting_sources user/project/local (types.py:2297-2307), local plugins (types.py:855-862), skills (types.py:2309-2329), subagents via agents (types.py:107-127, 2291-2295) and hooks. Codex: none found (case-insensitive search for 'codex' returned no matches).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code found in the SDK: nothing under src/ uses httpx/requests/urllib/socket (searched). All model traffic comes from the spawned CLI (subprocess_cli.py:873-881); that closed-source binary's own telemetry/update behavior is not checkable here. Accounts: the CLI needs Anthropic credentials - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, the macOS Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials', or an apiKeyHelper in user settings (_internal/session_resume.py:53-55, 326-386; e2e-tests/README.md:7-15); the README does not describe auth. Child env: SDK sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE=1 (subprocess_cli.py:819-825, 858-861); CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP can tag the User-Agent (types.py:2135-2136). If opentelemetry-api (extra 'otel') is installed and a span is active, W3C trace context is injected into the child env; no exporter is shipped (subprocess_cli.py:827-851). On connect it runs `claude -v` locally (2 s timeout) unless CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK is set (subprocess_cli.py:809-810, 1164-1224). With session_store set, transcripts are copied to the user-supplied backend (types.py:1609-1650). Build/release-time network: claude.ai/install.sh download (scripts/download_cli.py:245-272), pypi.org queries (build-and-publish.yml:165-176).

entry_points.what: query(): async generator for one-shot or streaming-input runs (hooks, can_use_tool and SDK MCP servers also work here)
ClaudeSDKClient: stateful client (query, receive_response, interrupt, set_permission_mode, set_model, rewind_files, stop_task, get_mcp_status, get_context_usage)
Public API (__all__ at 622-772): tool, create_sdk_mcp_server, session list/get/rename/tag/delete/fork (+ *_via_store), SessionStore, InMemorySessionStore, option/message types, errors
SubprocessCLITransport: locates and spawns the claude binary, frames its NDJSON stdout; the only shipped transport
Claude Code CLI executable (claude.exe on Windows); exists only inside platform wheels, git-ignored in the repo
run_session_store_conformance(): harness for validating SessionStore adapters
Release tooling CLI (with download_cli.py, update_version.py, update_cli_version.py) that builds platform wheels with the bundled CLI
Reference SessionStore adapters for S3, Redis and Postgres; 'Not packaged, not maintained as production code'

code.architecture: Thin Python control layer around the closed-source Claude Code CLI; no model-provider code exists in the package. Modules: _internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py - SubprocessCLITransport resolves the CLI (bundled _bundled/claude first, then PATH and fixed paths: 255-354), builds flags (--tools, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --model, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd, --permission-mode, --resume=, --settings with merged sandbox JSON, --mcp-config, --session-mirror: 570-795), spawns it with anyio.open_process incl. options.user and merged env (797-915), frames NDJSON stdout (163-221, 1097-1162), reaps children at exit (54-68). _internal/query.py - Query: control protocol (initialize with hooks/agents/skills, can_use_tool and hook_callback handling, mcp_message routing, interrupt/set_model/set_permission_mode/rewind_files/stop_task) and run-end/stdin-close logic (309-363, 577-704, 784-868, 1041-1091). _internal/sdk_mcp_bridge.py + _mcp_compat.py - in-process MCP servers over mcp's in-memory transport (mcp 1.x and 2.x). _internal/message_parser.py + types.py - JSON to dataclasses (messages, blocks, ClaudeAgentOptions, hook/permission/sandbox/session-store types). _internal/client.py (query()) and client.py (ClaudeSDKClient) - wiring. Persistence: the CLI writes JSONL transcripts under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects; session_store.py (InMemorySessionStore), transcript_mirror_batcher.py (batched/eager mirroring), session_resume.py (store-backed resume into a temp config dir), sessions.py, session_mutations.py, session_import.py, session_summary.py (list/read/rename/tag/delete/fork/import). Sandbox, permission evaluation, tool execution and subagents run in the CLI; the SDK forwards configuration only. No worker pool, queue or scheduler: each query()/ClaudeSDKClient owns one CLI subprocess.
code.packaging_and_release: Hatchling backend; wheel holds only src/claude_agent_sdk, sdist adds tests, scripts, examples, README, LICENSE (pyproject.toml:1-3, 62-77). SDK 0.2.163 (pyproject.toml:7), bundled CLI pinned 2.1.286 (_cli_version.py:3). Triggers: a push to main with commit message 'chore: bump bundled CLI version to ...' after the Test workflow passes auto-bumps the patch version (.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:3-17, 31-38; RELEASING.md:30-47); or manual 'Publish to PyPI' dispatch with a version after tests (Python 3.10-3.13) and lint (publish.yml:3-9, 12-58, 75-85). Both call build-and-publish.yml: wheels on 5 runners (manylinux_2_17 x86_64/aarch64, macosx_11_0 arm64/x86_64, win_amd64), each fetching the pinned CLI through https://claude.ai/install.sh, bundling it, recompressing with hash-pinned zopfli (build-and-publish.yml:17-37, 78-84; scripts/build_wheel.py:104-143, 466-497; scripts/download_cli.py:245-300; scripts/requirements-recompress.txt:4-8). Publish job: sdist (no CLI), PyPI quota/size pre-flight (wheels over 100 MiB are skipped), twine upload with the static PYPI_API_TOKEN secret, version commit pushed straight to main via SSH deploy key, optional Claude-generated changelog (continue-on-error), tag vX.Y.Z and GitHub Release (build-and-publish.yml:45-273; RELEASING.md:19, 71-77). PRs touching build files run build-wheel-check.yml (5-wheel dry run, platform-tag and bundled-CLI checks, import smoke test: build-wheel-check.yml:5-97). Checksums, signatures, attestations, SBOM: none found - a search for attest/sigstore/cosign/sha256/checksum/provenance/gpg/slsa/sbom hit only the zopfli requirement hashes and unrelated words; the downloaded installer is only shebang-checked (scripts/download_cli.py:124-134) and the CLI binary is not hash-verified.
code.tests_and_ci: pytest with anyio plugin (pyproject.toml:79-85). tests/: 36 test_*.py files plus conftest.py, about 1,079 test functions (grep count), run under asyncio and trio (tests/conftest.py:7-9); cover transport, query/control protocol, client, parsing, SDK MCP bridge, sessions/store/resume/mirroring, build scripts and example adapters (S3/Redis via moto/fakeredis; Postgres and live suites skip without SESSION_STORE_* env vars: examples/session_stores/README.md:30-44). e2e-tests/: 18 test_*.py files, 48 test functions, marked e2e, need real Anthropic API access and spend tokens (e2e-tests/README.md:5-15, 45-51; e2e-tests/conftest.py:19-28). Sandbox settings are covered only by command-construction unit tests (tests/test_transport.py:1807); no e2e test enables the sandbox (e2e-tests/test_tool_permissions.py:75-76 is a comment). mypy strict and ruff configured (pyproject.toml:87-149). Workflows: test.yml (unit on ubuntu/macos/windows, Python 3.13, Codecov; mcp==1.23.0 floor job with mypy; e2e on 3 OSes and in Docker via Dockerfile.test; example scripts; e2e jobs use GitHub OIDC workload identity federation and skip forks), lint.yml (ruff, mypy), publish.yml, build-wheel-check.yml, build-and-publish.yml, auto-release.yml, pypi-quota-check.yml (daily), claude.yml / claude-code-review.yml / claude-issue-triage.yml (Claude-powered repo automation), slack-issue-notification.yml.

code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md (nor CONTRIBUTING or CODEOWNERS) in this repository; .github/ holds only actions/ and workflows/. Hardening shows up only in code comments, e.g. refusing .bat/.cmd CLI paths on Windows (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py:414-448) and equals-form flag binding against flag injection (subprocess_cli.py:642-655).

claim_checks.claim: The Claude Code CLI is automatically bundled; the SDK uses the bundled CLI by default (README.md:15).
claim_checks.evidence: Code tries the bundled binary first (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py:255-260, 341-354), but it exists only in platform wheels: git-ignored (src/claude_agent_sdk/_bundled/.gitignore:1-3) and wheels are built for 5 targets only - manylinux_2_17 x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64/x86_64, win_amd64 (.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml:21, 78-84). The sdist has no CLI and an over-100-MiB wheel is dropped in its favor (RELEASING.md:19). Without a bundled CLI the SDK searches PATH and fixed paths, else raises CLINotFoundError (subprocess_cli.py:262-339).

claim_checks.claim: For a system-wide install or specific version, install Claude Code separately or set cli_path (README.md:15-18).
claim_checks.evidence: cli_path is honored (src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:2099-2103; subprocess_cli.py:237-239, 802-803), but a separately installed claude on PATH is consulted only if no bundled binary is found (subprocess_cli.py:257-264), so with a platform wheel it is ignored unless cli_path is set.

claim_checks.claim: Unlike query(), ClaudeSDKClient additionally enables custom tools and hooks (README.md:102).
claim_checks.evidence: query() passes hooks, can_use_tool and SDK MCP servers into the same Query object (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/client.py:100-107, 140-156); _configure_can_use_tool is documented as shared by query() and ClaudeSDKClient.connect() (types.py:1926-1935); Query keeps stdin open for one-shot runs that have them (_internal/query.py:1041-1087); an e2e test runs query() with a PreToolUse hook (e2e-tests/test_run_end.py:58-79; CHANGELOG.md:26). Code wins; the real difference is that query() cannot interrupt or take follow-ups (src/claude_agent_sdk/query.py:24-28).

claim_checks.claim: By default Claude has the full toolset; allowed_tools only auto-approves; disallowed_tools blocks (README.md:59).
claim_checks.evidence: SDK side matches: allowed_tools = auto-allow (src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:1985-1994), disallowed_tools = removed from the model's context (types.py:2063-2068), a separate tools option sets the base set (types.py:1974-1983); flags are emitted only when set, so the default adds no restriction (subprocess_cli.py:591-617). The tool list and enforcement live in the closed CLI, not checkable here.

claim_checks.claim: Custom tools are in-process MCP servers running inside your Python application (README.md:106-108).
claim_checks.evidence: create_sdk_mcp_server builds a regular mcp.server.Server (src/claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:491-619) served over an in-memory transport (_internal/sdk_mcp_bridge.py:1-22); CLI calls arrive as mcp_message control requests routed in-process (_internal/query.py:656-674, 753-782). Not in README: server-to-client sampling/elicitation/roots/logging/progress are not forwarded (types.py:648-659; sdk_mcp_bridge.py:103-112).

claim_checks.claim: Hooks are Python functions the Claude Code application invokes at points of the agent loop (README.md:201).
claim_checks.evidence: Callbacks are registered by id in the initialize request (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py:318-337) and run on hook_callback control requests (query.py:640-654); events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, Notification, SubagentStart, PermissionRequest (types.py:284-295); matchers on one event run concurrently (types.py:2182-2186).

claim_checks.claim: Release workflow takes claude_code_version (e.g. latest), creates a release branch and opens a PR to main (README.md:355-369).
claim_checks.evidence: publish.yml has only a version input (.github/workflows/publish.yml:3-9). The CLI version is the pin in _cli_version.py and the build rejects moving tags such as latest when reading it (scripts/build_wheel.py:90-125; scripts/_cli_version_validation.py:18-20). build-and-publish.yml commits the bump and pushes directly to main, then tags and releases - no branch or PR (build-and-publish.yml:231-273); RELEASING.md:5 agrees. README section is stale; code and RELEASING.md win.

claim_checks.claim: Use is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service (README.md:377).
claim_checks.evidence: LICENSE is the MIT license (LICENSE:1-21) and pyproject.toml says license MIT with an MIT classifier (pyproject.toml:11, 18); the README says Commercial Terms govern unless a component's own LICENSE file differs, without saying whether the MIT file is that exception. The repo holds no license text for the bundled CLI binary (src/claude_agent_sdk/_bundled/ contains only .gitignore).

claim_checks.claim: In-process SDK tools give 'No IPC overhead for tool calls' (README.md:151).
claim_checks.evidence: They avoid a separate MCP server process, but every call still crosses the SDK-CLI stdio channel as an mcp_message control_request plus control_response (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py:656-688; _internal/sdk_mcp_bridge.py:1-22). The repo publishes no measurement of the benefit.

claim_checks.claim: ResultError carries structured fields for a terminal error result (README.md:266-285).
claim_checks.evidence: ResultError subclasses ProcessError and exposes subtype, errors, result, api_error_status, terminal_reason, session_id, data (src/claude_agent_sdk/_errors.py:56-117); it replaces the generic exit-code error when the CLI already reported an error result (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py:268-273).

risks: Model scope: no GPT/OpenAI/'Sol' reference anywhere in the repo (searched). model is documented as a Claude model (src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:2070-2074), per-agent models are sonnet/opus/haiku/inherit or a full id (types.py:116-117), and usage provider values are Claude-serving providers plus a generic 'gateway' (types.py:1333-1336). All inference goes through the closed-source CLI (not in this repo); options.env is passed to it (types.py:2124-2137) but nothing documents pointing it at a non-Claude model.

Scope: a client wrapper, not a worker runtime or research harness. No pool, queue, scheduler or remote-worker management; each query()/ClaudeSDKClient owns one CLI child process, with an atexit SIGTERM reaper (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py:54-68, 873-882). No citation model: text blocks keep only `text`, and extra block fields and unrecognized block types are dropped by the parser (types.py:954-958; _internal/message_parser.py:168-208). Research would depend on Claude Code web tools that this repo only references (types.py:914, 987-996).

Sandbox limits: off by default, bash commands only, macOS/Linux; allowUnsandboxedCommands defaults True; enableWeakerNestedSandbox for Docker 'reduces security' (src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:919-928). Filesystem/network limits for other tools rely on permission rules (types.py:910-917). permission_mode bypassPermissions skips can_use_tool (types.py:1868-1874). Enforcement is in the closed CLI; this repo tests only command construction (tests/test_transport.py:1807) and no e2e enables it. In fresh checkouts the CLI ignores project-scoped permission grants until the workspace is trusted (scripts/trust_workspace.py:4-17).

Release integrity: wheels embed a closed-source CLI fetched at build time by running https://claude.ai/install.sh with only a shebang check, no checksum or signature verification (scripts/download_cli.py:124-134, 245-272). No signing, attestations, SBOM or provenance in workflows (only zopfli is hash-pinned: scripts/requirements-recompress.txt:4-8). Publishing uses a static PyPI token with twine and a direct push to main via deploy key (.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml:219-229, 258-261); build/twine/wheel are installed unpinned (line 31).

Moving target: every bundled-CLI bump auto-releases an SDK patch (RELEASING.md:30-47; most of CHANGELOG.md:3-100 is CLI bumps), so CLI behavior shifts under patch versions. The CLI's default model changed between releases and broke CI (e2e-tests/conftest.py:7-16; CHANGELOG.md:8, 42), so model needs pinning. Classified Alpha (pyproject.toml:16); Transport ABC may change or be removed (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/__init__.py:11-14); CI never runs Python 3.14 (.github/workflows/test.yml:22; publish.yml:16).

Licensing/governance: README says Commercial Terms govern (README.md:377) while LICENSE and pyproject say MIT (LICENSE:1; pyproject.toml:11, 18); no license text for the bundled CLI binary in the repo. No SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING or CODEOWNERS exists.

Persistence caveats: default is local JSONL under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/sessions.py:122-141). S3/Redis/Postgres adapters are 'Not packaged, not maintained as production code' (examples/session_stores/README.md:3); mirroring is best-effort - a batch is dropped after 3 attempts and surfaced as MirrorErrorMessage (types.py:1631-1650; _internal/transcript_mirror_batcher.py:32-35). session_store cannot combine with enable_file_checkpointing (_internal/session_store_validation.py:40-45); a custom Transport skips store-backed resume and ignores model, cwd, permission mode and tools options (query.py:63-70). Store-backed resume writes a temp config dir holding a copy of .credentials.json (refresh token removed), ~/.claude.json and settings.json, and may read the macOS Keychain (_internal/session_resume.py:167-176, 326-386, 431-454, 495-529).

Docs/code drift: README's client-vs-query and release-workflow statements contradict the code (see claim_checks); README never mentions sandbox, resume/session_store, model selection or auth. ClaudeAgentOptions.user is documented as 'an optional user identifier associated with the session' (types.py:2189-2190) but is passed to anyio.open_process(user=...) as the child's OS user (subprocess_cli.py:880; tests/test_transport.py:1756-1803). ClaudeSDKClient cannot be shared across async task contexts (client.py:58-64). e2e-tests/README.md cites a nonexistent test_mcp_calculator.py (line 55) and API-key secrets (line 78) while test.yml uses workload identity federation (test.yml:131-150).
